references.text: Pharaoh refuses to let all the Israelites go and drives Moses and Aaron away from him, continuing his sarcastic remark in verse 10.
Pharaoh attempts to limit the departure of the Israelites, similar to his resistance to letting the children leave in this verse.
Pharaoh again offers a compromise to let the people go but wants to keep back the livestock, showing his continued resistance.
God's promise to be with Moses stands in contrast to Pharaoh's sarcastic use of 'The Lord be with you' in this verse.
The expression about evil or trouble before one's face is used similarly to describe an impending danger.
The term 'רָעָה' (evil/trouble) refers to a looming danger that waits, parallel to Pharaoh's warning.
Contrastive parallel: The same blessing formula ('may the Lord be with you') used by a believer (Jonathan) versus an hostile ruler (Pharaoh's servant), highlighting the intention behind the words.
